_comment: Item #38 phase E supply-chain manifest (threat T7). Each entry pins the exact ffmpeg AND ffprobe binaries this app trusts for that RID by SHA-256 — scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.{sh,ps1} downloads and verifies against this file at build time, and FfmpegLocator.VerifyIntegrity re-checks them at every startup. An ffmpeg mismatch fails closed (no job endpoints served); an ffprobe mismatch or a missing ffprobeSha256 fails SOFT (item #70 phase 158) — the sidecar simply doesn't advertise the probe/thumbnails capabilities and the browser keeps doing that work in wasm.
_schema: url/sha256 are REQUIRED; everything else is optional. 'sha256' and 'ffprobeSha256' are the hashes of the EXTRACTED BINARIES — that is what FfmpegLocator.VerifyIntegrity hashes at startup, so the fetch scripts verify the same thing. 'archiveSha256'/'ffprobeArchiveSha256' are the hashes of the DOWNLOADED ARCHIVES, checked before anything is extracted so a tampered download is rejected without ever being unpacked (item #70 phase 174 — before this the scripts compared the archive against 'sha256' and would have contradicted the runtime check the first time a real pin was used). 'ffprobeUrl' is only needed when the source publishes ffprobe as a separate archive; when it is absent the scripts look for ffprobe inside the ffmpeg archive.

win-x64._comment: Item #70 — the Windows pin. Source: BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, static (non-shared) GPL variant so the install is two files rather than a folder of DLLs, build line n9.0.1 to match the macOS pins' 9.0. IT MUST BE A MONTH-END TAG, and that is the point of this note. The first pin here used a dated autobuild (2026-08-18-15-03), chosen over the rolling 'latest' tag because 'latest' would change under the hashes below. It went 404 within five weeks: BtbN keeps only about thirty daily builds. What it ALSO keeps, apparently indefinitely, is one build per month — the releases list still carries every month-end back to 2024-10-31 — so a month-end tag gives a URL that stays put AND a hash that never moves. Re-pinned 2026-09-20 to the 2026-08-31 build after the old one vanished, which had left fetch-ffmpeg unable to run on a fresh clone; nothing else was holding the build up, because ffmpeg/ is gitignored. If this 404s again, take the newest month-end tag from https://api.github.com/repos/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases and re-record all three hashes. NOTE: these hashes were recorded from the download, not checked against an independent publication of them — trust-on-first-use. The GPL licence is fine for distributing the installer ourselves; for the Microsoft Store the win64-lgpl variant of this same release is the one to use — it carries libopenh264, h264_mf and libkvazaar, all three tested on 2026-09-20 and all three do produce video, but it has NO libx264/libx265, so ArgvFactory's codec AND quality mapping must change with it (it passes x264's -preset and -crf, which none of the replacements accept).

osx-x64._comment: Pinned 2026-09-05 so an Intel Mac build could actually be produced — this entry was a TODO placeholder, so scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.sh osx-x64 failed and installer/macos/build.sh osx-x64 refused for want of a bundled ffmpeg. Same source as osx-arm64 (ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de), chosen for the same reasons: native static builds at immutable per-build paths with their own .sha256 files alongside. Both archives were checked against those published hashes before extraction, and both binaries are Mach-O x86_64. The version is 9.0.1 rather than arm64's 9.0 because that is what the source had built for amd64; each RID pins independently and nothing requires them to match.

osx-arm64._comment: Item #70 phase 174 — the first REAL pin in this file, added so the sidecar could be tested against genuine ffmpeg instead of Ben.Video.Sidecar.FakeFfmpeg. Source: ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de, chosen for macOS/arm64 because it publishes native arm64 static builds at immutable per-build paths with their own .sha256 files alongside (evermeet.cx, the placeholder this replaced, ships x86_64 only). ffmpeg and ffprobe are separate archives here, which is why 'ffprobeUrl' exists. Verified locally: Mach-O arm64, ffmpeg 9.0, encoders libx264/libx265/aac/libmp3lame/libopus, muxers mp4/webm/matroska.
